_readme: Configuration for the two spec generators, build_interface_docs.py and
build_spec_flow_diagram.py. Before this file existed both had one specification's
structure compiled into them as literals: heading strings, section numbers, entity
role sets and label ranges. Adding the v2 spec meant editing Python to publish a
Markdown change, which is the wrong shape and was tracked as delivery task T2.
Select a target with --spec KEY (default: the `default` key below).
Label ranges are NOT authoritative here. Each spec declares its own families in its
Notation table, and the generators read that table and cross-check it against the
`label_note.families` listed below. A range that drifts fails the build with the
spec's value and this file's side by side, rather than publishing a stale claim.

v1.title: CaRB3 per-site decarbonisation — v1, frozen COMIT-parity baseline

documents.title: CaRB3 Per-Site Decarbonisation — Input Data Model
documents.blurb:
Every entity the model reads: the premise record and its long companions,
the reference tables the modelling team maintains, and the optional per-site
intelligence that replaces an assumption with a fact where it exists.
documents.audience:
**Who this is for.** Anyone supplying data to the model — principally the
CaRB3 building-stock team, who own §3.1 and its companions. §1.6 of the
specification states the same contract as a requirement with rationale, and is
the better starting point if you are deciding *what to collect*; this document
is the normative field-level detail you validate against.

documents.title: CaRB3 Per-Site Decarbonisation — Output Data Schema
documents.blurb:
Every table a run produces, its keys, its units, and the traps that make two
of them look interchangeable when they are not.
documents.audience:
**Who this is for.** Anyone consuming results — analysts, aggregation code,
and anyone comparing one run against another. The evidence-tier and confidence
fields are not decoration: they are the only way to tell how much of a result
rests on a measurement rather than on a default, and §10 has validation tests
that exist solely to keep them honest.

v2.title: CaRB3 site energy system — v2, proposed, partially written

interfaces.blocked_by: T14 owns §7 and §6-§13 are unwritten, so there is no §8 output schema to publish. §3 alone would ship a half-contract whose companion link is dead.

documents.title: CaRB3 Site Energy System — Input Data Model
documents.blurb:
The nine entities of the carrier/duty/unit spine: what flows, what needs it,
and what converts between the two.
documents.audience:
**Who this is for.** Anyone supplying data to the v2 model. This is a
proposed contract against an unbuilt system — v1 remains the COMIT-parity
baseline and its interface documents are the ones in force.

diagrams.blocked_by: T13 owns §4; it is a stub with no `### A1 — ` headings, so the journey diagram and the SVG flow would both come out empty.
